source.data:
@api
Feature: Shop API
  Backend scenarios. Every step's HTTP exchange appears in the report attached to the step that
  made it - method, URL, status, latency, headers and bodies, with secrets redacted.

  Scenario: The catalogue lists every product
    When I request the product catalogue
    Then the response status should be 200
    And the catalogue should contain 4 products

  Scenario: A known product can be fetched by SKU
    When I request the product "GADGET-2"
    Then the response status should be 200
    And the product name should be "Gadget"

  Scenario: An unknown SKU is a 404, not a crash
    When I request the product "NOPE-9"
    Then the response status should be 404

  @secrets
  Scenario: Logging in returns tokens that must never reach the report
    # The password deliberately does NOT appear here. SpecReport redacts captured traffic, but
    # it renders step text exactly as written - a credential typed into a feature file will show
    # up in the report, because it is part of the test rather than part of the traffic.
    When I log in as "ada"
    Then the response status should be 200
    And the response should contain an access token

  Scenario: An out-of-stock item cannot be added to the basket
    When I add "DOOHICK-3" to the basket via the API
    Then the response status should be 409

  @restsharp
  Scenario: RestSharp traffic is captured exactly like HttpClient
    When I request the product catalogue using RestSharp
    Then the RestSharp response status should be 200

  @known-fail
  Scenario: A failing assertion shows the exchange that produced it
    When I request the product catalogue
    Then the catalogue should contain 99 products

source.data:
@ui @api @fullstack
Feature: Full stack
  The scenarios this whole sample exists for: a single scenario that talks to the API *and*
  drives the browser, so one timeline carries HTTP exchange panels and screenshots side by
  side. No special casing - the report attaches whatever evidence a step produced.

  Scenario: An item added through the API shows up in the storefront
    Given the basket is empty via the API
    When I add "WIDGET-1" to the basket via the API
    And the storefront is open
    Then the basket count should be 1
    And the basket total should be "9.99"

  Scenario: The storefront and the API agree on the catalogue
    Given the storefront is open
    When I request the product catalogue
    Then the number of products on screen should match the API

  @known-fail
  Scenario: A mismatch between UI and API is visible from both sides
    Given the basket is empty via the API
    When I add "GADGET-2" to the basket via the API
    And I add "GIZMO-4" to the basket via the API
    And the storefront is open
    Then the basket count should be 5

source.data:
@ui
Feature: Shop storefront
  Frontend scenarios driven by Playwright. Screenshots are captured on failure by default, so a
  failing step carries a picture of the page as it was.

  Background:
    Given the storefront is open

  Scenario: The catalogue renders every product
    Then I should see 4 products listed

  Scenario: Searching filters the list
    When I search for "gad"
    Then I should see 1 product listed
    And the first product should be "Gadget"

  Scenario: Out-of-stock items cannot be added
    Then the "DOOHICK-3" add button should be disabled

  Scenario: Adding an item updates the basket
    When I add "Widget" to the basket
    Then the basket count should be 1

  @known-fail
  Scenario: A failing UI assertion captures a screenshot
    When I search for "gizmo"
    Then I should see 3 products listed
